scoring.recency: 0–1h = 2.3 (breaking) · 1–3h = 2.0 (fresh) · then linear decay to 0 by 24h · unknown = 0.5
scoring.signal: AI/tech (or watchlist) keyword hits — match_count capped at 5 × 0.6
scoring.source: outlet authority from trusted-sources.md: primary (company/lab) 2.0 · citation 1.2 · screening 0.5 · other 1.0
scoring.corrob: cross-outlet corroboration — how many outlets ran the same headline (cluster_size − 1, capped 3) × 0.8

candidates.description: New Microsoft Copilot Brings Home, Code, and Autopilot Together    Microsoft Source
candidates.body_text: Category: Company News 25/09/2026 New Microsoft Copilot Brings Home, Code, and Autopilot Together 2 minutes New capabilities bring AI-powered work, automation, and application development together in a single platform. The new Copilot is centered around Home, Code, and Autopilot. Home and Code will be rolled out gradually to the Microsoft Frontier program over the coming weeks. Autopilot will expand to Private Preview at the end of the month. In addition, Microsoft is integrating Word, Excel, and PowerPoint directly into Copilot and offering a preview of upcoming capabilities such as Today in Home and @Copilot in Teams. The most important key points: “Home” brings Chat and Cowork together in one central location. While Chat supports day-to-day work, Cowork enables users to delegate entire tasks. “Code” enables users to build applications and automations using natural language. The new capability is based on the same technology as GitHub Copilot and is designed to enable non-developers to securely create their own solutions within their organization’s environment. “Autopilot” works as an agent that can continue working on tasks independently, even when the user is away from their computer. Office directly integrated into Copilot: Files in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint formats can be created and edited directly in Copilot. candidates.title: Introducing the new Copilot with Home, Code and Autopilot
candidates.description: Introducing the new Copilot with Home, Code and Autopilot    The Official Microsoft Blog
candidates.body_text: Introducing the new Copilot with Home, Code and Autopilot Sep 25, 2026 | Jared Spataro - Chief Marketing Officer, AI at Work We’re reimagining Microsoft Copilot to enable work as it evolves and to help expand what every individual and every organization can accomplish in the flow of human ambition. Today we’re introducing the new Copilot to connect the tools people rely on with the next generation of capabilities they’ll need to build, customize and scale AI across work. The Copilot app now has three new capabilities: Home is your new starting point, where Chat and Cowork come together — and with Office in Copilot, the full power of Word, Excel and PowerPoint is now built into the experience. Code lets everyone build their own solutions with the tools to run them safely, and it’s powered by the same underlying technology as GitHub Copilot. And Autopilot is a persistent, proactive and personal agent that keeps working even when you’re not. Home and Code will start rolling out in our Frontier program in the coming weeks and Autopilot is expanding to private preview at the end of the month. We’re also excited to share new FinOps for AI capabilities to help you manage spend and get the most value from Copilot and agents. Image Credits: Lucas Ropek Hardware At Meta Connect, the company’s smart glasses were everywhere Lucas Ropek 6:08 PM PDT · September 25, 2026 If there was one thing that was obvious this from Meta Connect this year, it’s that the social media giant is all-in on its burgeoning line of smart glasses. Indeed, the glasses were pretty much everywhere at the annual event, where Meta shows off its newest hardware and AI products. Both Meta staff and the flocks of influencers who frequent the event seemed to arrive with the glasses glued to their faces. Most of the demos the company offered this week also involved the glasses. I swiftly joined the bespectacled masses and found myself trying on pair after pair of Meta’s high-tech specs. One of the more notable products I had an opportunity to demo were Meta’s new, still-unreleased, audio-only smart glasses . News of these glasses emerged not long after the company weathered accusations that it was selling “pervert glasses,” with critics alleging that its camera-equipped specs could be used for nefarious surveillance purposes. The new glasses come equipped with six microphones, but no camera, and they have no native way to record your surroundings, which should go a long way toward easing privacy concerns. candidates.body_text: PC Components CPUs Meta Muse runs agents on AMD EPYC Turin hosts with two cores and 8GB of memory — AI agent can pass terminal commands to Ubuntu host system News By Jake Roach Published 10 hours ago The 9D25 that hosts Muse comes with 126 cores and 254 threads. When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Share this article 10 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Recent updates Update 7:53PM ET: Added a tweet from Meta's David Singleton and a link to Muse's security paper. Meta's new AI agent Muse is powered by AMD EPYC Turin host systems, with each sandbox sporting two dedicated cores and 8GB of memory. Blogger Evan Hoffman and analyst Tae Kim both discovered that Muse will run some rudimentary Ubuntu commands if prompted, passing along the output to help identify things like the specs of the host system. More concerning is that Muse seems able to execute commands that might be unsafe, with Hoffman claiming that Muse offered to set up SSH to Muse's private VM. Imagine if one billion people used a personal AI agent.
